questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility to study at the University of Bologna, to live in Italy for a while and soak up the Italian culture & learn the Italian language. Especially the courses from the MA Psychology of Wellbeing and Social Inclusivity and Mediation since I want to combine Psychology and Film in my future career.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was impressed by my professors and their way of teaching.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I definitely had to organise everything by myself and some things were very confusing - especially regarding the possibility of choosing subjects of Psychology as a student of the Humanitarian department. I had a lot of calls with Unibo and KU to make sure everyone was on the same page because I received a lot of contrary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance via email by the Exchange Student Desk. No assistance by my exchange coordinator Unibo.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. I was lucky to find something through a friend of a friend who did Erasmus in Bologna some years ago. She passed me a contact. Many other students could not arrive in Bologna because they were not able to find something. Recommendations: Look for something very very early, ask people who lived there already to get contacts, Facebook groups, be prepared that a lot of agencies rent out rooms and charge additional agency cost.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is definitely nice to have a shared household with other internationals or Italians. If you can, find an appartment with Italians so you learn the culture and language even better.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have a check in to proof that you have arrived in Italy, you have some forms to fill out, you have to go to the University to print your student card.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Via email and phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end it was successful, even though I would have liked to join only Psychology classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose the subjects you are interested in and if you need help, call them. Sometimes it takes a while to get a response via email. Prepare everything earliest as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The effort you have to do is quite a lot but it is worth it - the courses I had very incredibly interesting and a high level of professionalism.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The host university focused a lot on different teaching methods - movies, discussions, lectures, etc combined with presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Humanitarian Communication
Mediation in German
Cognitive Styles and Wellbeing
Developmental Psychology and Wellbeing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Humanitarian Communication was one of the best courses I have ever had - it is incredibly important to learn about it because it focuses on contemporary and prospective societal challenges and how we should talk about them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Volleyball, Basketball once a week
A lot of parties and travel opportunities by ESN

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want to do sports, take adavantage of the sports classes. You can also join a local team (I did tennis) next to the offers from the University

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the trains and go to the cities close to Bologna, a lot of places are very close and it is cheap to travel by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the city is very international and the Italians are very open and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join sports classes, go to bars and cafés to meet new people, go to the library to study - you will always see similar faces.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming and friendly attitude from the Italians, the eating and enjoyment culture. They also appreciate it a lot if you know some phrases in Italian and they see you want to learn them.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Look for accomondation very early 
- Choose courses also from different departments than your own
- Be open and ready for new learnings, new friendships and new opportunites

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sometimes things seem a bit messy and chaotic but relax and take it easy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The knowledge I gained from the courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning to know that you do not have to be part of everything and to know that the right people will come to you at the right time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
